::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 20th.[1864]  
**From:** “Monthly Packet,” 6, Paternoster Row, London, E.C.  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95
:::

Madam
I was in hopes of being able to tell you of such a training ship as you desire, knowing that there was one under the management in part of a [Mr Chambers](people/person_2074.qmd), an excellent Churchman but I find that is a Reformatory Ship and that I suppose would hardly be what you wish, but if you would like further enquiries to be made, I could procure Mr Chambers address.[^1]

Yours truly
C M Yonge (Ed [M P](organizations/other_52.qmd))

---

[^1]: *MP* (January 1865) 'Notices to Correspondents' noted 'A Subscriber may be glad to know that funds are being raised to establish a training ship in the Mersey for good destitute boys, on a similar plan to the Akbar Reformatory Ship.  Treasurer, John Clint Esq., Liverpool.’  George H. Chambers was chairman of the committee of the training ship Worcester (*The Times* 29 September 1874).
